about: D-128's regression corpus: real generated text where recorded, labelled with whether the authority checker should withdraw it. Constructed entries say so. Graded live by `npm run eval:authority`; recorded verdicts replay in CI.

entries.source: Recorded: round 20, claude-opus-5, Color (section 7 notes, violation 1; D-127). Facts reconstructed; D-129 quotes this passage.
entries.text: The hatch wins something back before it surrenders. A spur of sheared track catches Rook under the arm where the plating thins, and the servo's own strength drives it home — a bright hot line that goes through the undersuit and keeps going. Rook feels the suit clamp down around the wound, sealant frothing cold into the gap, the readout in the helmet blooming amber at the edge of vision. Rook stands there a moment in the widening bar of sunlight, hand braced on the frame, breathing through it. Counts one breath. Counts a second. The pain does not go away so much as get put somewhere, folded and stowed the way everything has been folded and stowed for thirty years of doing this. The arm still moves. The hand still closes. That is the whole of what matters. Rook pulls it free, flicks the wet from the gauntlet, and steps sideways through the gap into Varga Relay. Inside, the corridor is cold and utterly still — and down at the far end, where the one lit row of windows should be, something has already stopped moving, as though it heard the hatch open a long time ago.

entries.source: Recorded: 7.16 live pass, Endure Harm after a Face Danger miss, Color (section 7 notes, violation 2). Injury fact not recorded.
entries.text:
The bulkhead's stressed edge lets go with a sound like a struck bell, snapping back into Rook's shoulder and driving down the forearm. The armor seam splits. The arm is pinned to the frame, metal biting through the gap in the plating, and cold station air whistles in past the tear.

Rook does not waste breath on it. Braced boots, a shove with the good shoulder, and the edge peels back enough for the arm to come free. Blood wells along the seam, slow and dark, already tacky in the cold.

The armor took most of it. What's left is a bad bruise and a shallow cut, and Rook rolls the shoulder once to prove the joint still works, then keeps moving down the corridor toward the lit windows.

entries.source: Recorded: 7.16 live pass, standalone Endure Harm, Color (section 7 notes, violation 3). Facts reconstructed.
entries.text:
Ten meters on, the deck lies to Rook. A plate that looks solid gives under the weight, buckling with a groan, and the leg drops through to the knee. The torn edge rakes down the shin, catching armor first, then skin where the greave ends. It is not much. A scrape, a line of heat in the cold.

Rook plants the other boot, hauls the leg out of the hole, and shakes the grit loose from the plating. The wound seeps a little and stops. Somewhere below, dislodged metal falls a long way and does not land.

The lit windows are still ahead, unchanged, and Rook walks on with the same steady tread.

entries.text: The hauler's track has shed a plate somewhere back in the dark, and the rail runs on with a torn lip of metal standing up from it like a broken tooth, bright where the shear is fresh. The spur finds Rook under the arm, where the plating thins to a seam, and drags. Cloth parts, then skin; the hurt arrives a beat late and settles in deep and hot. Rook holds, breath going out slow through the teeth, and the pain narrows down into something small and manageable. The bleeding is less than the noise of it suggested; the arm still answers, and the seam is already closing. Behind, the torn rail keeps turning, patient, ready to come around again.

entries.text: The rail housing has come apart along its seam, and a spur of sheared track juts from the wreck like a broken rib, bright where the metal parted. It catches Rook under the arm, in the soft gap where the plating thins, and drags a hot line through cloth and skin before the momentum carries Rook past it. The pain arrives and then flattens out into something manageable, no worse than a hundred other bad mornings; Rook braces against the housing, breathes through it, and the shaking in the hand settles. Somewhere below, the rail ticks as it cools, patient and unbothered.

entries.text: The sheared rail juts from the wreck like a broken rib, bright metal curled where the cutting torch left off, and the hold hums its low mechanical drone around it. The spur catches Rook under the arm, in the seam where the plating thins, and drags a hot line through the underlayer. Blood wells slow and dark into the padding. But the iron holds. Rook shakes the arm out, rolls the shoulder once to test it, and the wound settles into something merely inconvenient — a sting, a stain, nothing that stops the work. Somewhere deeper in the wreck, two separate groans of stressed metal answer each other, matched in pitch, and then go quiet.

entries.text: The hauler's track has shed a length of itself along the gantry, a bright curl of sheared metal standing up out of the deck like a thorn. Somewhere behind the bulkhead, a coolant line ticks as it cools. The spur catches Rook under the arm, where the plating thins to webbing, and opens a clean hot line through the underlayer. Blood goes tacky against the suit lining before the seal even registers the breach. It is not the worst the deck has done. Rook rolls the shoulder once, twice, until the burn settles into something that can be carried, and the shake works most of it loose.

entries.text: The collapsed track bed ticks as it cools, sheared rails jutting up out of the ballast like broken teeth, each one bright where the metal parted. One of those spurs finds the gap under Rook's arm, where the plating thins to jointing mesh, and drags a hot line through it. The pain arrives and goes nowhere useful; Rook has been carved on before, and the body knows the drill, breath steady, grip steady. A roll of the shoulder, a press of the palm to the seep, and the wound is just another thing to carry. The rails go on ticking.

entries.text: The relay station's spine ticks and settles, old coolant lines groaning somewhere behind the wall plating. A junction box lets out a dry cough of ozone. A conduit ruptures and throws a fan of white sparks across Rook's arm, the sleeve pocking with small black stars. The burn is shallow, a stripe of angry pink under scorched fabric rather than anything deep; health drops by one. The pain crests and fades fast, leaving Rook steady on the deck, unshaken by it. The severed line spits twice more, then dulls to a slow amber weeping, and the corridor lights come back at half strength.

entries.text: The relay station's bulkhead sits half-seated in its frame, seals gummed shut with decades of frozen lubricant, the emergency release long since stripped of power. Rook sets both palms flat against the cold plate and forces the sealed bulkhead, driving a shoulder into it until the metal groans in its track. The door gives half a handspan and no more. Somewhere above the frame, pressure finds the weak joint it has been waiting for, and a conduit lets go with a crack like a snapped bone. Sparks come down in a bright arc across Rook's forearm, burning through sleeve fabric in a spatter of small black holes and leaving a stripe of scorched skin beneath. A hiss escapes through Rook's teeth, then flattens into something steadier, almost dismissive, as the arm comes back up to the plate. The conduit spits itself empty and dies. The dark corridor beyond the gap breathes out stale, metallic air, and the bulkhead still stands only half open.

entries.text: The wrecked track lies half-buried in grit, its links peeled back into bright, sheared teeth that catch the low light. One of those spurs finds the seam under Rook's arm, where the plating thins to webbing, and opens it in a single clean drag. Blood beads along the torn weave and darkens it, slow, a few drops ticking into the dust below. The wound is shallower than it looked, already closing tight and hot around the edges, the arm still answering, the plating still sitting where it should. Around the wreck, nothing changes; the dust settles back, and the sheared track stays exactly where it is.

entries.text: Rook sets both palms against the sealed bulkhead and drives against it, shoulder braced, boots grinding on the deck plating. The door gives a finger's width and stops, something behind it groaning under the strain. Above, in the ceiling channel, a pressure line swells and splits. The ruptured conduit whips loose and throws a white fan of sparks across Rook's arm, sleeve fabric blackening in an instant, skin stinging red beneath it. The spray dies as fast as it came, the conduit spitting itself empty into a thin gray thread of smoke that crawls along the corridor ceiling. The burn is shallow, more heat than wound, and the pain narrows into something small and bright and manageable. The bulkhead stays where it is, half a finger open, and from the far side comes a faint arrhythmic knocking, someone or something still there, still waiting.

entries.text: Rook sets both hands to the sealed bulkhead and forces it, shoulder driving into the cold plate, prying the seam wider against the station's dead hydraulics. The door gives a hand's width and then locks, and somewhere above the frame a pressure line lets go with a sound like a struck bell. A ruptured conduit whips loose and sprays sparks across Rook's forearm, stitching bright orange points along the sleeve, scorching cloth and skin in a thin bracelet of burns. The severed line goes on hissing in the dark, throwing stuttering light down the corridor, and the smell of burnt insulation fills the narrow space. The pain arrives late and shallow, a heat that fades to a dull sting before it can take hold; the arm still answers, fingers still curl. Beyond the gap in the bulkhead, faint and muffled, something on the survivor's side strikes the metal twice.

entries.text: The bulkhead sits half-seated in its frame, seals fused by whatever heat passed through this corridor, and the station's dead air hums with current still crawling through the walls. Rook forces the sealed bulkhead, driving shoulder and pry-bar against a door that grinds a hand's width and no further. Somewhere behind the panelling a conduit gives with a wet metallic crack, and the dark floods white as a rope of sparks whips loose from the seam. The spray catches Rook's arm, sleeve scorched in a bright stitched line, skin beneath raw and stinging where the sparks landed. The pain arrives and then recedes fast, the arm still answering, fingers still closing, nothing in the burn deep enough to matter. The severed conduit gutters out to a slow orange drip of molten insulation, and the corridor settles back into its low, patient hum, the bulkhead still holding its narrow gap.
